query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Electroless deposition of a nanoscale copper shell onto tungsten powders prior to spark-plasma sintering (SPS) will produce a W–Cu composite with a continuous Cu network and fully wetted W/Cu interfaces, eliminating interfacial voids and increasing thermal conductivity relative to an identical SPS baseline without Cu shell plating.
generation.material_initial_state: Blend of polycrystalline W powders (10–50 µm) and Cu powders (5–20 µm); W powders coated by electroless Cu deposition to ~100–200 nm thickness
generation.intervention: Electroless Cu plating of W powders followed by SPS at 1000–1100 °C under 50 MPa uniaxial pressure in vacuum for 10 min
generation.conditions: SPS in vacuum (<10 Pa), die temperature 1000–1100 °C, pressure 50 MPa, hold 10 min; post‐sinter service at 500–900 °C under thermal fluxes up to 10 MW/m² and irradiation up to 10 dpa
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous nanoscale Cu shell on each W particle that melts during SPS to form a fully connected Cu network and intimate W–Cu interfaces
generation.mechanism: Upon heating, the Cu shell liquefies at temperatures well below W sintering temperature, flows and wets neighboring W particles, eliminating voids and promoting densification without W grain growth; the resulting microstructure features minimal porosity and maximized Cu conduction pathways
generation.predicted_outcome: Composite thermal conductivity increases by ≥30% and open porosity reduces to <2 vol% compared to SPS of uncoated powders
generation.baseline: SPS of mechanically mixed 50:50 vol% W–Cu powders under identical conditions without Cu shell plating
generation.boundary: Valid for SPS temperatures 950–1150 °C, pressures 30–70 MPa; service in vacuum or inert environments at 500–900 °C and irradiation ≤10 dpa
generation.uncertainty: Degree of improvement depends on uniformity and continuity of electroless Cu shell and on Cu evaporation or oxidation during SPS

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of 50:50 vol% W–Cu powder batches: one with W powders electrolessly plated with 150 nm Cu shell, one without plating. SPS both batches at 1050 °C, 50 MPa, 10 min in vacuum.
measurements: Bulk density and open porosity via Archimedes method and SEM image analysis
Thermal conductivity by laser flash diffusivity
Interfacial bonding quality via SEM and focused‐ion‐beam cross-sectioning
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plated‐powder composite does not show ≥20% higher thermal conductivity and porosity ≤4 vol% (vs baseline), the hypothesis is falsified.
